title: Pizza Bianca with Ricotta and Vegetables
subtitle: White pizza with creamy ricotta, courgette and mozzarella
excerpt: Pizza bianca skips the tomato sauce and lets ricotta and mozzarella take the lead. Thinly sliced courgette roasts on top as the pizza bakes, picking up colour at the edges. The dough is a simple hand-mixed white dough that only needs 20 minutes to rest.
sourceNotes: Pizza bianca (white pizza) is a Roman street food tradition. Without tomato, the focus shifts to high-quality cheese and toppings. The style is popular across Rome and southern Italy.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dough can be made up to 24 hours ahead and kept in the fridge, covered. Bring to room temperature before shaping.
recipe.temperatureNote: Use the highest setting your oven allows, ideally with a pizza stone or upturned baking tray preheated inside.

content.text: A very hot oven is the single most important factor. Place a baking tray in the oven while it heats up. Slide the pizza onto the hot tray to get a crisp base from underneath.

items.prepNote: very thinly sliced on a mandoline or with a peeler

content.text: You will also need 7g fast-action dried yeast, 1 tsp fine salt, and 300ml warm water for the dough.
Mix the flour, yeast, and salt in a large bowl. Add 300ml warm water and 2 tablespoons olive oil. Mix to a rough dough.
Knead for 8 minutes on a lightly floured surface until smooth and springy. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 240C with baking trays inside.
Divide the dough into two pieces. Roll each out as thin as you can on baking paper.
Spread ricotta over each base. Scatter over mozzarella, courgette, garlic, and thyme. Drizzle with remaining olive oil.
Slide each pizza (on its paper) onto a hot baking tray. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the edges are golden and the base is crisp.
Finish with lemon zest just before serving.

items.symptom: Base is soft and doughy in the centre.
items.cause: Oven or tray was not hot enough.
items.fix: Preheat tray for at least 20 minutes before baking.

items.cause: Slices were too thick and released water.
items.fix: Slice very thin; pat dry with kitchen paper before using.
